name: es20-depth-test
title: Depth buffer test
summary: Eight depth functions, write mask (also for glClear), clear value, depth range, polygon offset and gl_FragDepth, verified through which of two overlapping quads wins; plus initial-state and round-trip queries.
spec: ES 3.0 §2.13.1 Controlling the Viewport (DepthRangef, window-space z)
ES 3.0 §3.9.2.3 Shader Outputs (gl_FragDepth is clamped, not remapped by the depth range)
ES 3.0 §4.2.2 Fine Control of Buffer Updates (DepthMask)
ES 3.0 §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers (ClearDepthf; clears obey masks and scissor)
ES 3.0 §4.3.2 Reading Pixels (only color is readable: depth is observed through colors)
ES 3.0 §4.4.5 Effects of Framebuffer State on Framebuffer Dependent Values (DEPTH_BITS)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.6 Variance and the Invariant Qualifier
GLSL ES 3.00 §7.1 Vertex Shader Special Variables (gl_VertexID, gl_Position)
GLSL ES 3.00 §7.2 Fragment Shader Special Variables (gl_FragDepth, gl_FragCoord)

api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST on/off decides whether depth is tested and stored (cell 8); POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL on/off decides whether glPolygonOffset applies (cells 14-15); SCISSOR_TEST confines clears (cells 10-11)
api.glDisable: same states; a disabled depth test passes a farther fragment and stores nothing; FILL disabled leaves a coplanar decal losing LESS
api.glIsEnabled: DEPTH_TEST and POLYGON_OFFSET_FILL: initially FALSE, TRUE after glEnable, FALSE after glDisable
api.glDepthFunc: all 8 functions x 3 fragment depths (nearer/equal/farther than the stored 0.5) = 24 pixel probes against a CPU truth table; GL_DEPTH_FUNC read back for all 8
api.glDepthMask: FALSE: a passing fragment's color lands but its depth is not stored (later 0.4 fragment still passes), TRUE stores it; FALSE also makes glClear(DEPTH) a no-op; GL_DEPTH_WRITEMASK read back
api.glDepthRangef: same NDC z gives different window z in four stripes (default, [0.5,1], [0,0.5], reversed [1,0]) and flips the LESS outcome; GL_DEPTH_RANGE read back incl. clamping of (-1,2) to (0,1); gl_FragDepth-vs-range rule observed with a documented radeonsi deviation
api.glClearDepthf: four bands cleared to -3, 0.4, 0.6, 5 (clamped to [0,1]) decide whether a 0.5 fragment passes LESS; GL_DEPTH_CLEAR_VALUE read back incl. clamping
api.glClear: COLOR|DEPTH per cell; scissored DEPTH-only clears; glClear(DEPTH) with DepthMask(FALSE) leaves the stored depth untouched
api.glClearColor: cell background color observed where a failed fragment leaves the cleared color
api.glPolygonOffset: negative units lets a coplanar decal win LESS, positive units makes it lose LEQUAL, factor scales the depth slope of a tilted quad (factor -8 wins, -0.25 and units-only lose); POLYGON_OFFSET_FACTOR/UNITS read back
api.glViewport: per-cell viewport maps the quads to the probed pixels
api.glScissor: restricts the depth clears of cells 10 and 11 to a half / quarter of the cell
api.glUniform2f: per-quad depth (u_depth) and gl_FragDepth line (u_depth_line) observed through depth outcomes
api.glUniform4f: quad rectangle and color observed in the image
api.glUseProgram: plain and gl_FragDepth programs both rendered the probed pixels
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE readback of the 56 probe pixels (via Check::expect_pixel and read_pixel)

visual_review.notes: 256x256 radeonsi capture: 4x4 grid of blue cells separated by black lines. Row 0: NEVER all blue, LESS green stripe only, EQUAL yellow only, LEQUAL green+yellow. Row 1: GREATER magenta only, NOTEQUAL green+magenta, GEQUAL yellow+magenta, ALWAYS all three stripes. Row 2: test-off cell shows a magenta left stripe and green/orange right stripe; depth-mask cell has orange over the yellow (mask off) left stripe and green right; masked-clear cell blue left / green right; clear-value cell dark with green only in the right half. Row 3: depth-range cell green/blue/green/blue; gl_FragDepth cell with green, orange-over-blue, green and a green/blue ramp; offset cells show the coplanar decals (green and yellow win, others blue) and a single green decal in the tilted cell. Matches the CPU truth tables; no artifacts at cell borders. On radeonsi the third gl_FragDepth stripe is green (documented clamp-to-depth-range deviation); llvmpipe shows it blue.
